description: The decision to ship build_first_valid_path as an iterator-driven retry loop on top of build_path_candidates is correct. A future contributor will look at this and suggest one of: (a) folding the retry into build_path itself ("why have two helpers?"); (b) building it into PathCandidates ("why have a separate function?"); (c) replacing it with a single full-pool validate_all-paths function. All three are wrong: (a) breaks build_path's backward-compat contract and forces a SignatureVerifier dep on every build_path caller; (b) puts policy/verifier into an iterator that should be pure topology, violates the separation of concerns the trait surface enforces; (c) loses the lazy-yield property that lets adversarial-pool callers stop early. The layered shape — pure topological iterator, single-shot first-yield wrapper, signature-verifying retry helper — is the right factoring and worth defending in PR review threads.
title: build_first_valid_path is the right shape: iterator + per-candidate validate_path retry
